title: GReFEM: Multimodal LLMs as Zero-Shot Semantic Assistants for Physics-Guided 3D Mesh Refinement
claim: A multimodal LLM can localize critical regions from rendered views, and those regions then flow through staged modules into 3D refinement anchors.
layout: Single row, left-to-right; inputs feed MLLM, then four stage boxes with example outputs below
description: A left-to-right pipeline diagram. On the left, rendered 3D views of a servo-motor CAD part, with a grid overlay, sit above an orange label box ('3D Views + Top k GReFEM Views'). Beneath it are two white rounded boxes holding the physics instruct prompt and the grid-marking instruction. Arrows lead into a green hexagonal brain icon labeled MLLM. A curly brace leads from the MLLM to four colored stage boxes along the top: purple Region Proposal, red Feature Detection, blue MV-RaySeg, yellow Mesh Generation. Each stage has a rounded output panel below it. These show the MLLM's text output listing edges, contours, holes and fillets per view, then cropped grid cells with red markers, then ray-projection math with 3D renderings, then a dense triangulated mesh of the part. The eye goes first to the MLLM brain and then to the colored stage boxes.
caption: GReFEM Pipeline: We process the top views V∗, via the Region Proposal and Feature Detection Pipelines. Once the points Q are obtained on the views, we use our Surface Projection (2D to 3D) pipeline to obtain anchor points P for mesh generation.
abstract: Adaptive volumetric finite element meshing traditionally requires iterative PDE solvers or heavily supervised, data-driven surrogates trained on large-scale simulation data. This work explores a significant question: can the high-level semantic understanding of off-the-shelf MLLMs serve as a viable, zero-shot geometric proxy for finite element mesh refinement? We introduce $\textbf{GReFEM}$ (Geometric Reasoning Enhanced Multimodal LLMs for Finite Element Meshing), a framework that utilizes MLLMs to visually localize stress-critical regions based on physics-guided textual prompts. To bridge the gap between 2D MLLM pre-training and 3D geometries, we introduce $\textit{orthoViews}$, a trained view-selection module that assists these MLLMs by maximizing the observability of key geometric features. We evaluate $\textbf{GReFEM}$ by computing finite-element error at stress concentrations, on diverse CAD mesh geometries under multiple loading cases, with MLLMs and prompt variants, against blind and load-informed geometric heuristics, solver-informed Zienkiewicz--Zhu (ZZ) refinement, and a retrained learned adaptive-meshing baseline, all at a matched element budget. Without any FEM solve or simulation training data, $\textbf{GReFEM}$ lowers the critical-region peak von Mises stress error relative to a blind geometric heuristic and to refinement driven by a coarse FEM solve, closing $58\%$ of the gap between the unrefined mesh and a reference-solve oracle, while a hand-derived analytical load-informed heuristic remains stronger and the learned baseline performs slightly better overall. With this we investigate their performance as semantic assistants in automated simulation workflows. Code is available at https://github.com/kbali1297/GReFEM
